admission.workflow: Resolve four complete immutable Proctor themes over one static semantic-token catalog, retain mature color parsing and composition, and atomically project namespaced values plus density, motion, transparency, and contrast state into a renderer root.

items.rationale: The canonical Microsoft MIT text is preserved as the local notice for the transferred source and owner test.
Preserve complete RGBA, HSLA, HSVA, luminance, contrast, blending, transparency, color-space conversion, named-color, parse, and format behavior.
Preserve the four color-scheme identities and dark/high-contrast classification helpers.
Run the complete color owner suite through the admitted test adapter; one unsupported assertion helper is expressed as two exact hue assertions without reducing the obligation.

Retain current-theme access, ordered change events, themable lifecycle, and root application behind a narrow browser service that has no file, product-icon, extension, environment, or dynamic participant authority.

VS Code's mutable extension-facing color registry, theme JSON schema, and dynamic theming participants would violate Proctor's static packaged token authority; complete color math remains admitted through the base color module.
Informs the root-theme projection boundary; Proctor publishes only its generated --prctr-* variables and explicit presentation attributes.

dependencies.rationale: The admitted base runtime supplies lifecycle and ordered event behavior.
The design-system icon catalog consumes the same root presentation contract without exposing glyph or theme authority.

divergences.summary: One immutable Proctor catalog owns lowercase dotted semantic tokens and deterministic --prctr-* names; extensions, remote content, settings documents, arbitrary registrants, and VS Code JSON theme contributions cannot add or override tokens.

Only light, dark, high-contrast light, and high-contrast dark records are admitted; every record must resolve every token before any root mutation, and high-contrast elevation uses explicit boundaries instead of shadow.

Density, motion, and transparency selections affect only resolved visual tokens and root attributes; reduced motion resolves duration roles to zero and reduced transparency removes backdrop alpha without changing product or security state.

verification.obligation: Run the complete upstream suite for color construction, conversion, luminance, contrast, blending, formatting, parsing, transparency, and regression cases.
Verify four immutable complete themes, stable namespaced CSS variables, contrast, high-contrast elevation, and explicit compact-density mappings.
Verify root theme switching, one ordered event, high-contrast state, compact density, zero reduced-motion duration, and opaque reduced-transparency backdrop in sandboxed Chromium.
Verify layer direction, static imports, cycle ownership, CSS ownership, and production composition boundaries.
Verify schema, local digest, marker, license reference, unique ownership, divergence, and evidence parity without a VS Code checkout.
Resolve the exact VS Code commit and verify every reviewed upstream blob against the canonical checkout.
